gappers.catalyst: CoreWeave Q3 beat (EPS -$0.95 vs -$1.53 est, revenue $3.66B vs $3.54B est, ~170% YoY), backlog $132.5B and FY26 revenue guidance raised to $13.2B, with funding plans outlined — but five analysts cut price targets the same morning
headlines: CoreWeave Posts Solid Q3: Analyst Can 'Almost Hear the Sigh of Relief' (Benzinga, 34 min ago)
CRWV Stock Surges 15% Pre-Market as CoreWeave Touts $133 Billion Backlog — But Short Seller Jim Chanos Warns of Weak Returns on Capital: '2-3% Pre-Tax ROIC' (Benzinga, 1 hr ago)
CoreWeave's AI Boom Splits Wall Street: One Analyst Sees a Hurricane, Another Sees a Turning Point (Benzinga, 2 hrs ago)
gappers.catalyst_detail: CoreWeave reported Q3 2026 after the close on Nov 10: EPS -$0.95 against a -$1.53 estimate and revenue $3.66B against $3.54B consensus, roughly 170% YoY growth, with revenue backlog at ~$132.5B and full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to ~$13.2B. Net loss was still $709M and cash burn remains heavy. Management also outlined funding plans, which mattered more than the beat: CRWV's unsecured 2030/2032 notes had been trading above 15-16% yields in early November, levels widely read as distressed. The CEO separately flagged a ~$10B revenue opportunity from re-leasing older Nvidia GPUs without new capex. Wall Street split hard — Evercore cut $150 to $100, Truist $165 to $115, Cantor $176 to $100 and Stifel $120 to $60 on the morning of the beat, while Jim Chanos publicly argued the business earns only 2-3% pre-tax ROIC.
gappers.why: The beat plus an explicit financing plan de-risks the 'AI circular financing' fear that had been the sector's dominant bear case — OpenAI's ~$300B Oracle commitment and ~$22.4B of CoreWeave contracts are funded with debt, so CRWV's cost of capital was being treated as the whole chain's solvency test. Clearing that test triggered a relief squeeze into a very crowded book: 23.82% of float short at only 1.07 days to cover, in a stock that closed $48.74 against a 52-week range of $40.58-$138.25.
gappers.impact: Reads as a relief bounce off the lows rather than a trend change. Premarket volume 1.75M on the Alpaca scan (Benzinga showed 12.06M by 08:52 ET) against a 42.08M average daily — not volume-confirmed for a 13% gap. RSI 44, still below neutral. The tell against durability is that the same analysts who acknowledged the beat cut their targets to $60-$115 on the day, i.e. the Street treated the print as relieving near-term funding risk without fixing the returns-on-capital problem. Sector read-through is broad and is the direct cause of three other names on today's list: BE (+7.69%), NBIS (+11.62%) and ORCL (+5.25%) are all trading on this print, not on news of their own.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The guidance raise and backlog are genuinely structural, but the stock is still ~60% off its high with distressed-level bond yields and a same-day sweep of target cuts — the relief is about financing timing, not a resolved thesis, so it is a days-long squeeze rather than a multi-week swing.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing on the book to displace — 0 positions, $100,000 cash, 0/3 weekly trades used (week of Nov 9). The real cost is the queued XLV limit-buy (108 sh into $182-186) for tomorrow's market-open run: CRWV would burn one of three weekly slots and swap a low-beta defensive rotation entry for the highest-beta name on the board. On R:R it fails at a sane stop: ATR14 is $6.11 (11.1% of price), so a 1-ATR stop sits at $49.16, an 11.1% loss that breaches the -7% manual-cut rule outright. Tightening to the -7% cut ($51.40) puts the stop inside half an ATR of noise and needs $63.01 for 2:1 — above Stifel's fresh $60 target. Entry is barred regardless: +13.4% trips the no-chase rule.

gappers.catalyst: Pure CoreWeave read-through as the closest listed neocloud comp — Nebius reports its own Q3 tomorrow (Thu Nov 12) before the open, so the gap is sympathy plus pre-earnings positioning
headlines: NBIS, CRWV Stocks Pull Back After Post-Earnings Rally; Analysts Stay Firmly Optimistic About Cloud Opportunity (Stocktwits)
Nebius secures $3.5 billion; FY26 contracted capacity guidance raised to 5 GW (Unusual Whales / company disclosures)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No Nebius-specific news today. CoreWeave's Q3 beat and raised full-year guidance read straight across to Nebius as the nearest listed neocloud comparable, lifting it ~11.6% off a $133.96 close. Nebius's own Q3 2026 print lands tomorrow, Thu Nov 12, before the open with the call at 8:00 AM ET; consensus is roughly a $0.69/sh loss on ~$907.5M revenue against $146.1M revenue and -$0.40 EPS a year ago. Company-specific context from the prior fortnight: FY26 contracted capacity guidance raised to 5 GW and $3.5B of financing secured. The stock is still ~40% below its record.
gappers.why: A peer's guidance raise de-risks the shared sector thesis that AI-infrastructure demand justifies the capex and debt load, so money rotates back into the whole neocloud complex just ahead of the next print. Amplified by positioning — roughly 22% of float short at ~2.2 days to cover means a sector bid forces covering into a thin premarket book. None of the information is Nebius's own.
gappers.impact: A one-day sympathy spike with a binary event stapled to it, not a trend change. Premarket volume ~558k against a ~20.7M average daily is no confirmation. Technicals contradict the tape: price sits below both the 20-SMA (~$158) and well below the 50-SMA (~$199), with MACD below signal and RSI in the mid-40s. The sector read-through is explicit and two-way — CRWV's print is the cause, and both names re-price together on tomorrow's result. Reference levels: ~$168.50 resistance, ~$146 support.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst belongs to another company and expires in under 24 hours when Nebius itself reports — holding past tomorrow's call converts a momentum trade into an unhedged earnings bet.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 positions, all cash, 0/3 weekly trades). Cost is one of three weekly slots plus the queued XLV entry, swapping a mid-cycle defensive sleeve for a high-beta name held through a print. Fails 2:1 at any sane stop: the $146 support stop is only ~$3.50 away, far inside an ATR14 of $16.45 (11.0% of price), so it gets taken out on routine noise; widen to a true 1-ATR stop ($133.08) and 2:1 demands ~$182, well above the $168.50 resistance. The no-chase rule settles it anyway at +11.6%.

gappers.catalyst: Benzinga states it plainly: Bloom Energy jumped ~9% premarket after CoreWeave earnings fuelled a broad rebound in AI-infrastructure plays — layered on genuine own-company contract wins (Google 702-MW role Nov 6, NTT DATA 900-MW agreement Nov 5)
headlines: Why Is Bloom Energy Stock Surging Wednesday? — stock jumped nearly 9% premarket after CoreWeave earnings fueled a broad rebound in AI infrastructure plays (Benzinga, 1 hr ago)
Bloom Energy Scores Major Role In Google's 702-Megawatt Power Project (Benzinga, 5 days ago)
NTT DATA Announces Agreement with Bloom Energy for 900 MW of Onsite Power Generation Across Multiple Data Center Projects (Business Wire, Nov 5)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Today's gap is sympathy — Benzinga's mover note attributes it directly to CoreWeave's print lifting the AI-infrastructure complex, and BE had fallen 4.36% on Tuesday to $185.42 before it. But unlike the other sympathy names on this list, Bloom carries dated, company-specific structural wins from the prior week: a 900-MW onsite power generation agreement with NTT DATA across multiple data-center projects (Nov 5) and a major role in Google's 702-MW power project (Nov 6). Fundamentals back it up — Q3 2026 (Oct 22) delivered EPS $0.94 against a $0.65 estimate. Sell-side remains well above spot: consensus PT $241.41, RBC maintaining $335 on Nov 9, Barclays upgrading Nov 3. Valuation is the caveat at a 112x P/E on a $58.9B market cap.
gappers.why: Fuel-cell onsite generation is the shovel-seller to the data-center buildout, so anything that re-rates AI capex durability re-rates Bloom's order pipeline. CoreWeave's funding plan removed the near-term 'capex gets cancelled' fear, and Bloom is the most direct listed beneficiary with signed megawatts already on the board. Note the short base is small (6.81% of float, 1.06 days to cover), so this is a demand bid rather than a squeeze — a higher-quality move than CRWV's or NBIS's.
gappers.impact: The most sustainable-looking move on today's list, though still thinly confirmed: premarket volume 345k on the scan (882k on Benzinga) against a 15.55M average daily. RSI 44, and price sits mid-range in a wide 52-week band of $75.70-$351.28. The sector read-through is the same AI-power complex that moved OKLO today, but Bloom is the one with revenue and signed contracts behind it rather than a 2028-29 deployment timeline. Sector classification also matters here: Industrials / Electrical Equipment, which is a favored sleeve in the early-cycle row of the strategy's rotation table — the best rotation fit of the five.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The NTT DATA 900-MW and Google 702-MW awards are structural multi-year revenue, not headlines, the company is beating on earnings, and Industrials aligns with the early-cycle rotation phase — this is the one name here worth a multi-day/week swing hold if it later clears the Confluence rule on a /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 positions, all cash, 0/3 weekly trades), so the cost is one weekly slot and the direct comparison with the queued XLV entry — BE is higher beta but, unlike XLV, has a dated same-day catalyst and sits in a favored early-cycle sector. Against today's own list it ranks below CRWV and NBIS on gap size but above both on quality of move (demand-driven, not short-covering; own contracts, not a peer's print). R:R is the only setup here that clears the minimum cleanly: ATR14 $18.98 (9.5%), so a -7% cut at $185.73 lands almost exactly on Tuesday's $185.45 close as real support, risking $13.98 against a $241.41 consensus target for roughly 3:1, and 2:1 needs only $227.67. The blocker is entry timing, not geometry — +7.69% trips the no-chase rule, so this is a pullback-to-$186 watch item, not a chase.

headlines: Oklo Seeing Solid Execution as it Shifts From Design, Wedbush Says — Groves-1 test reactor operational, progress on Aurora-ID construction (MarketScreener, Nov 9)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No Oklo-specific headline is dated today. The nearest is a Nov 9 Wedbush note framing Oklo as shifting from design to execution, citing the Groves-1 test reactor becoming operational and construction progress on the Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory, with first deployment still 2028-29 and ~1 GW targeted by 2031-32. Q3 2026 landed Nov 6 pre-open — a modest beat on a tiny base (EPS -$0.22 vs -$0.26 est, revenue $1.86M vs $1.11M) alongside a wider net loss. Today's gap tracks the macro bid and the AI-power complex rather than anything Oklo published.
gappers.why: A high-beta pre-revenue name near its lows mechanically over-recovers when the tape turns risk-on, and roughly 21% of float is short at ~4.9 days to cover — a much slower unwind than CRWV's 1.07 days — so a sector bid squeezes a crowded, hard-to-exit book. This is beta and positioning, not new information about the reactor business.
gappers.impact: A mean-reversion bounce inside a severe downtrend. Premarket volume ~450k against a ~10.2M average daily is weak confirmation for a 7% gap. The stock remains far below its 52-week high and the analyst trend is actively deteriorating — six target cuts in three weeks (Canaccord, B. Riley, Truist, Citi, Barclays, TD Cowen) make the headline consensus a stale lagging number. Read-through is the AI-power complex, which is why it moved with BE and CRWV today rather than with utilities.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Macro beta plus a short squeeze with no company news today, and the genuine structural catalyst (first Aurora deployment) is 2028-29 — far too distant for a swing hold, and it sits awkwardly against the rotation table where this pre-revenue name trades like speculative tech rather than a utility.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 positions, all cash), so the cost is the weekly trade budget and the ranking against today's own list — OKLO is the weakest of the top five on catalyst quality (no same-day news at all) with a visibly deteriorating analyst trend, and it is strictly dominated by BE, which shares the AI-power thesis but has signed contracts and revenue behind it. It also competes with the queued XLV entry, a better rotation fit. R:R geometry is workable: ATR14 $1.91 puts a 1-ATR stop at $24.96, ~7.1% below the print and almost exactly on the -7% manual cut, so 2:1 needs $30.69 — not absurd. But the entry gate fails on three counts: +7.07% trips no-chase, there is no documented same-day catalyst as the Confluence rule requires, and buying a name this far off its high on macro beta alone is the bottom-fishing the strategy forbids.

gappers.catalyst: No Oracle-specific news — CoreWeave read-through via the OpenAI financing chain (OpenAI's ~$300B five-year Oracle commitment), bouncing off a 52-week low after five straight negative sessions
headlines: Steve Eisman: Oracle Could Suffer if OpenAI 'Demise' Causes US Recession — sees a 70% chance the AI boom ends in a bear market or worse (Benzinga, Nov 10)
Oracle Stock Nears Death Cross as Microsoft Deal Unwinding Points to More Risks (Benzinga, Nov 7)
Oracle Stock Slides as Microsoft Reportedly Pulls Back From AI Computing Deal (Benzinga, Nov 6)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nothing from Oracle today; the gap is entirely CoreWeave read-through. Oracle sits in the same AI financing loop — OpenAI has committed roughly $300B over five years to Oracle, and Oracle priced $10B of bonds alongside a $10B share sale in early November to fund its data-center buildout. CoreWeave clearing its funding test therefore relieves Oracle's own financing overhang by association. Oracle's own recent news flow is uniformly negative: Microsoft reportedly pulling back from an AI computing deal (Nov 6), the stock approaching a death cross (Nov 7), and Steve Eisman warning on Nov 10 that Oracle suffers if OpenAI falters, with a 70% chance the AI boom ends badly. The stock closed $117.98, down 1.51%, against a 52-week range of $109.21-$250.25. Next earnings are not until Dec 9.
gappers.why: Mechanical sympathy through a shared counterparty. The market had been pricing Oracle as a levered proxy on OpenAI's solvency, so a peer demonstrating it can still raise money compresses that risk premium. Note there is no squeeze component — short interest is just 2.37% of float — so this is real buying off an oversold base rather than forced covering, but it is also the thinnest-conviction catalyst on the list because none of the information is Oracle's.
gappers.impact: Most likely a one-day oversold bounce that mean-reverts. Premarket volume 855k against a 33.30M average daily is very weak confirmation. RSI 46, and the stock is a few dollars off a 52-week low in a confirmed downtrend with a death cross pending — a bearish structural signal that today's gap does nothing to repair. The headline consensus PT of $250.91 is a lagging number: Goldman cut $240 to $206 and Wells Fargo $280 to $250 in late October. The unresolved Microsoft pullback is company-specific damage that no CoreWeave print addresses.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A peer's earnings bounce with no Oracle catalyst of its own, against an unresolved Microsoft contract loss and an imminent death cross — the structural story here is deteriorating, not resetting, and the next company catalyst is a month away on Dec 9.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (0 positions, all cash, 0/3 weekly trades). Within today's own list ORCL is the lowest-ranked and the weakest case — it has the smallest gap, the thinnest volume confirmation relative to average, no catalyst of its own, and the only actively deteriorating company-specific storyline (Microsoft). It would displace both the queued XLV entry and the better-supported BE setup. Sizing is also the least efficient: ATR14 $7.53 implies 132 shares, a $16,388 notional at 16.4% of equity, consuming most of a 20% position cap for the weakest thesis. R:R is nominally workable — a -7% stop at $115.46 risks $8.69 and needs $141.53 for 2:1, below even the cut targets — but a stop at $115.46 sits only ~6% above the 52-week low in a death-cross downtrend, so the geometry flatters a setup the chart does not support. +5.25% trips no-chase as well.
